Title: Selangor Wholesale Market operations continue despite fire
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Wholesale Market in Seri Kembangan is operating as usual, with business activities unaffected by a fire on July 23.
The Selangor Agricultural Development Corporation (PKPS) said the fire did not involve the main building housing daily operations and traders' activities, while the cause of the incident remains under investigation.
"The market area has been confirmed safe and daily operations are continuing as usual. PKPS has also activated a 24-hour Crisis Management Centre to monitor developments.
"PKPS will coordinate follow-up actions and work closely with the authorities to assist investigations into the incident," it said.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar confirmed the fire did not affect the main building and firefighting operations were completed at 6am yesterday.
Ashrul Riezal said the department's Investigation Division would begin its forensic probe on Monday after taking over the premises yesterday afternoon.
He said an initial assessment by investigation officers and the K9 Detection Unit had begun, but the unit had to temporarily suspend entry into the hotspot area due to high temperatures at the site.
"The preliminary cause of the fire, including any possibility of sabotage or negligence, is still being investigated by the investigation team," he said.
Yesterday, it was reported that 68 personnel and 16 fire engines were deployed during the operation, with support from 13 fire stations.
The operation also involved 67 personnel from 11 Volunteer Fire Brigades, as well as members of the police force, Subang Jaya City Council and the Selangor Wholesale Market security team.
Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim said business operations at the wholesale market continued as usual despite three shops within the compound being destroyed in the blaze. — BERNAMA

Title: PM: Malaysia's halal certification should be backed by industry capabilities
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Malaysia has the potential to emerge as a global halal industry hub if its internationally recognised halal certification system is backed by robust industry capabilities and strategic international collaboration.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the global recognition of Malaysia's halal certification system has opened up opportunities for the country to expand cooperation with nations seeking to develop their own halal industries.
He said several world leaders he had met had expressed interest in collaborating with Malaysia in the halal sector, including obtaining the country's halal certification.
"Chinese President Xi Jinping, Brazilian President (Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva) and South African President Matamela Cyril Ramaphosa, without exception, said Malaysia has achieved strong performance in the halal industry and that they want to work with us to obtain halal certification and recognition from Malaysia," he said when launching the Penang International Halal Expo (PIHEX) 2026 and the Penang Bumiputera Entrepreneurs Gathering (HUBPP) at Politeknik Seberang Prai in Permatang Pauh today.
However, Anwar said Malaysia could not rely solely on the strength of its halal certification, but must instead build a more comprehensive halal industry ecosystem.
"I want to emphasise that we should not focus only on halal certification. Our strength lies not only in certification, but also in creating synergy between certification and industry," he said.
He said collaboration between the government and industry was crucial to ensuring halal standards continued to be upheld while enabling local companies to penetrate global markets.
He added that the halal industry was no longer confined to food, but had evolved into a high-value economic sector encompassing a wide range of industries.
Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Penang Deputy Chief Minister I and Penang Halal Industry Development Council (MPIHPP) chairman Datuk Dr Mohamad Abd Hamid, and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.

Title: Lawyer files police report over alleged bullying at school linked to Zara Qairina case
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A lawyer representing a child in a bullying case involving the late Zara Qairina Mahathir has lodged a police report regarding another alleged bullying incident at the same school.
Datuk Ram Singh, who represents Student A in the Kota Kinabalu Children's Court and at the Coroner's Court inquest into Zara Qairina's death, lodged the report at the Luyang police station today.
He urged police to investigate whether relevant authorities implemented anti-bullying measures at the Papar school following the incident involving Zara Qairina, who was found unconscious on July 16 last year.
Ram said he made the report out of concern for the safety, welfare, and discipline of students at the school, where Zara Qairina's death remains the subject of an ongoing inquest at the Coroner's Court.
"I am deeply concerned after receiving information regarding another alleged bullying incident at the same school.
"Based on the information I obtained, the incident occurred on May 13, 2026, involving three male students. I understand the victim's father lodged a police report, an investigation was conducted, and the three students were charged at the Children's Court in Papar.
"I also understand that the court ordered all three students to perform 120 hours of community service at the same school," he said.
He described the incident as shocking, as it occurred while the inquest into Zara Qairina's death was still underway.
"This raises serious questions about whether there are shortcomings in the school's disciplinary system, supervision, hostel management, and overall monitoring of student welfare and safety.
"In this matter, I request the police to conduct a thorough investigation to determine whether there are elements of negligence, dereliction of duty, or any offences committed by responsible parties under relevant laws," he said.
He also requested police to examine whether there was a failure to comply with procedures, policies, or guidelines set by the Education Ministry, Sabah State Education Department, or school management in ensuring student protection.
Additionally, he urged police to investigate whether authorities had implemented necessary administrative approaches, monitoring mechanisms, and preventive measures following the previous incident to prevent similar disciplinary breaches.
"If the investigation reveals any negligence, breach of duty, or violation of law by any individual or responsible agency, I request that appropriate action be taken in accordance with the law," he said.
He said the report was made in the public interest to ensure student safety and welfare remain the top priority and to prevent similar incidents in the future.

Title: GPS device, fish finder for registered Melaka fishermen expected by end of August
Article:
MELAKA: Global Positioning System (GPS) technology devices and fish finders for use by registered fishermen in Melaka are expected to be obtained by the end of August at the latest.
State Rural Development, Agriculture and Food Security Committee chairman Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said that the use of the technology, which is expected to benefit around 1,000 fishermen, involves an allocation of RM1 million provided by the state government.
"We have completed the procurement process and now we are waiting for the delivery of the devices.
"The use of GPS and 'fish finder', estimated to be worth between RM1,100 and RM1,200, is hoped to increase the income of fishermen as it makes it easier for them to locate fish more accurately compared to conventional methods," he told reporters after launching the Melaka AgroFest 2026, which was also attended by Melaka Agriculture Department director Rozli Azizi Talib.
Dr Akmal said that the initiative is also expected to contribute to the modernisation of the state's fishing sector, in addition to helping fishermen plan their movements at sea systematically and to avoid entering restricted areas.
In another development, he said the state government through the Department of Agriculture has granted an exemption of nearly RM100,000 in Temporary Occupation Licenve (TOL) fees to farmers and breeders who cultivate idle state-owned land.
"This exemption is given from a one-year period from April this year until April next year, and we are still encouraging more farmers or breeders to cultivate idle state government land," he said.
Earlier, he said that Melaka Agrofest 2026 aims to attract around 50,000 visitors, with sales worth RM1.6 million, over the three-day event which began yesterday.
He said the annual event, which brings together farmers, breeders, fishermen, and agricultural entrepreneurs from all over Melaka, is not only to promote local agricultural products and agri-food but also to attract tourists from outside Melaka in conjunction with the Visit Melaka Year 2.0 this year.
Dr Akmal also said that 60,000 Melaka Jagung Manis cobs will also be distributed for free to Melaka AgroFest 2026 visitors throughout the three days.
In addition, he said that 14 categories of awards were given to farmers, breeders, fishermen, and agricultural entrepreneurs, involving a prize value of RM30,000 as an appreciation and to boost the spirits of these groups to continue contributing to the sector they are engaged in.

Title: Malaysia must intensify fight against drug abuse before we lose another generation
Article:
LETTER:
The persistent and growing problem of drug abuse in Malaysia is a matter of utmost seriousness and warrants national concern.
Despite decades of enforcement, rehabilitation programmes and public awareness campaigns, drug abuse continues to spread, particularly among young people.
The rapid emergence of synthetic drugs has made the challenge even more dangerous and complex.
We must ask ourselves an uncomfortable but necessary question: Are we fighting a losing battle against drug abuse?
The increasing prevalence of synthetic drugs, which are often cheaper, more potent and easier to produce than traditional drugs, has changed the landscape of drug abuse.
These substances can cause severe psychological disturbances, violent behaviour, hallucinations and permanent brain damage.
They are also more difficult for authorities to detect and regulate because their chemical composition can be altered to evade existing laws.
The sight of individuals wandering the streets in a confused, disoriented or aggressive state due to drug abuse is deeply disturbing. It is a tragedy not only for the individuals concerned but also for their families and for society as a whole.
Every "zombie" we see on our streets is a reminder that someone has fallen through the cracks of our prevention, treatment and enforcement systems.
This is no longer merely a law enforcement issue. It is a national public health, social, educational and security challenge that requires a comprehensive, whole-of-government and whole-of-society response.
While enforcement remains essential, we cannot arrest our way out of this problem.
We must address the root causes that make young people vulnerable to drugs, including mental health issues, peer pressure, family breakdown, unemployment, social isolation and the influence of organised criminal syndicates.
To strengthen our national response, I propose the following:
1.
Declare drug abuse, especially synthetic drug abuse, a national priority with stronger coordination among all relevant ministries and agencies.
2.
Intensify intelligence-led enforcement against drug trafficking syndicates, particularly those manufacturing and distributing synthetic drugs, while strengthening border security and disrupting online drug sales.
3.
Strengthen prevention programmes in schools, colleges and universities through continuous education that develops life skills, resilience and informed decision-making, rather than relying solely on fear-based campaigns.
4.
Expand mental health services for young people, recognising the close relationship between substance abuse and psychological distress. Early intervention and counselling should be readily available in educational institutions and communities.
5.
Empower parents and families with the knowledge and skills to recognise early warning signs of drug abuse and to seek timely assistance.
6.
Enhance community-based rehabilitation and aftercare services to reduce relapse rates. Recovery does not end when treatment ends; former addicts need employment opportunities, counselling, family support and community acceptance.
7.
Harness technology to monitor emerging drug trends, identify online trafficking networks and provide accessible digital platforms for prevention, counselling and reporting.
8.
Engage youth as partners in prevention efforts by supporting peer-led initiatives, youth ambassadors and community volunteer programmes that encourage healthy lifestyles and resilience.
Drug abuse is not just destroying lives — it is weakening families, undermining communities and threatening the nation's future workforce and productivity. If we fail to act decisively today, we risk creating a generation trapped in addiction, with far-reaching consequences for public safety, healthcare and economic development.
The fight against drugs cannot be left solely to the National Anti-Drugs Agency and the police. It requires the active participation of every stakeholder — government agencies, schools, employers, religious organisations, community leaders, civil society organisations, parents and young people themselves.
Malaysia has overcome many national challenges through unity and collective action. We must now demonstrate the same determination in confronting the menace of synthetic drugs.
The cost of complacency is simply too high.
The question is not whether we can afford to strengthen our response. The real question is whether we can afford not to.
Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye
Chairman, Alliance for a Safe Community

Title: KM Bendahara bolsters Malaysia's maritime capabilities in Sabah, South China Sea
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The deployment of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency's (MMEA) latest offshore patrol vessel KM Bendahara is expected to strengthen the country's enforcement, surveillance and operational readiness, particularly in the waters off Sabah and the South China Sea.
The vessel was officially named at the MMEA Bendahara Naming Ceremony, launched by Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman here today.
KM Bendahara is the former United States Coast Guard (USCG) cutter USCG Steadfast (WMEC-623), built in 1967 and retired from USCG service on Feb 1, 2024 after more than five decades of service.
The vessel was acquired by the Malaysian Government under the United States Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programme before being officially handed over to the MMEA on Sept 5, 2025 in Baltimore, the United States.
In his speech, Awang Alik said the commissioning of KM Bendahara demonstrates the Madani government's continued commitment to strengthening national maritime security by enhancing strategic assets to address increasingly complex security challenges.
Awang Alik said the government had allocated more than RM30 million to finance the vessel's maintenance and refurbishment, crew training, and delivery voyage to Malaysia as a strategic investment in enhancing the MMEA's operational readiness.
"Sabah remains a priority for the federal government in the national security agenda due to its position as Malaysia's frontline in the Maritime Zone and the strategically important South China Sea," he said.
Awang Alik also expressed appreciation to the entire KM Bendahara crew for successfully bringing the vessel home safely after completing a voyage of more than 49 days from Baltimore, which began on Sept 17, 2025.
"The historic voyage crossed seven seas, four major gulfs and two international straits before arriving in Klang on Nov 4, 2025, and subsequently in Kota Kinabalu on Nov 14, 2025.
"Throughout the voyage, the crew faced numerous challenges, including joint training with the USCG, technical disruptions and navigation signal spoofing incidents, all of which were successfully overcome through professionalism, mental resilience and strong teamwork," he added.
He said the ceremony also reflected the growing strategic relationship between Malaysia and the United States in maritime security, with the transfer of the vessel from the USCG to the MMEA symbolising the high level of trust placed in Malaysia as a strategic partner in safeguarding regional waters.
"KM Bendahara will operate alongside the MMEA's other offshore patrol vessels, including KM Tun Fatimah and KM Arau, to strengthen operational presence, patrols and enforcement in the South China Sea and Sabah waters," he said.
On the vessel's name, Awang Alik said Bendahara symbolises wisdom, authority, loyalty and trustworthiness, values that formed the foundation of governance during the Malay Sultanate era, and expressed hope that the name would inspire the ship's crew in carrying out their responsibility to safeguard the nation's maritime sovereignty.

Title: BN has no objection to TH RCI report release, says Tok Mat
Article:
SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional has no objection to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji being tabled in Parliament or released to the public if the Cabinet decides to do so.
Its deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the RCI report was an important investigative document prepared by a commission appointed by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, adding that any follow-up action arising from its findings was a matter for the government.
"If the Cabinet decides to do so, we have no problem with that.
"We have never objected to the RCI being made public, and neither have I. The report can be tabled in Parliament or released to the public, but it must follow proper procedures and receive Cabinet approval," he said after appearing on Podcast Utama Buletin TV3 in conjunction with the Negri Sembilan election.
He said any individuals found to have committed wrongdoing should face legal action, stressing that the matter had nothing to do with any political party.
Mohamad, however, questioned why the Tabung Haji RCI had become a major issue during the current election campaign, saying he did not see its connection to the Negri Sembilan polls.
"I don't understand why the Tabung Haji RCI has become such a hot issue during this election. I don't know what it has to do with Negri Sembilan.
"I don't know whether there is something hidden in the RCI report because I'm not privy to it. I do not have access to the document."
Responding to a question on why the report had not been released three years earlier, Mohamad said he was unable to explain the delay.
"I don't really understand why the decision was not made public. There have been other investigative reports that were also not disclosed," he said.
Mohamad said the decision ultimately rested with the prime minister and the Cabinet.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Thursday, after opening a forum in Kuala Lumpur, said the government may release the final report of the
RCI
into Tabung Haji.
Anwar told reporters the report could be released immediately if Cabinet approval was not required, or after the Cabinet meets next Wednesday.

Title: Kemas staff may get permanent positions under new service scheme, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA PILAH: The Community Development Department (Kemas) has been directed to prepare a new service scheme that will pave the way for its educators and staff to be appointed to permanent positions instead of remaining on contract.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who issued the directive, said he had instructed the Kemas director-general to prioritise the matter, including offering a more attractive salary package under the new scheme.
"I have instructed Kemas director-general Datuk Mohd Hanafiah Man to look into a new service scheme for all Kemas teachers, with better salaries and more attractive offers.
"The existing service scheme approved by the Public Service Department places Kemas teachers on contract.
"I have asked the director-general to ensure that all Kemas personnel are given permanent positions," said Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister.
He said this when launching the Negri Sembilan-level Hari Kemas and Alpha Gen Talent @Kemas programme here today.
Zahid said the move was not linked to the ongoing Negri Sembilan election campaign.
He added that Kemas had undergone significant transformation over the years and had earned international recognition through its Tabika and Tadika programmes.
He said Kemas had received recognition from Reader's Digest for six consecutive years, reflecting the dedication of its educators despite limited facilities in some areas.
"Kemas has shown over six decades that it should never be underestimated. The commitment shown by Kemas teachers and staff has earned global recognition, proving that we can continue to progress," he said.
Zahid also commended Kemas for strengthening early childhood education by introducing Quran literacy and memorisation programmes for young children.
"The aim is to nurture children with strong values, clear minds and the foundation to  excel academically in the future," he said.
Touching on skills development, Zahid said Kemas continued to play an important role by offering training programmes in areas such as tailoring, beauty services, cooking and entrepreneurship, which should be expanded for the benefit of rural communities.

Title: Teen's automotive dreams cut short in fatal Karak crash
Article:
TEMERLOH: The aspirations of 17-year-old S. K. Kiisven to pursue a career in the automotive industry were cut short after he died in an accident at Km 86 of Jalan Kuala Lumpur–Kuantan near Karak early today.
The victim's father, C. Sasi Kumar, 47, said his second child was pursuing a skills course at a vocational academy in Karak, Bentong.
"He had a keen interest in cars and motorcycles, which is why he enrolled in the automotive course in Karak. However, he always returned home every weekend," he said when met at the Sultan Ahmad Shah Hospital Forensic Medicine Unit here today.
Sasi Kumar said the last time he saw his son was at 1am at a temple near their home in Sungai Kawang, Lanchang, while preparing for a religious ceremony.
"I decided to head home early because I felt tired, then received a phone call at 4.30am informing me that Kiisven had been involved in an accident. I immediately rushed to the scene," said Sasi Kumar, who works as a plantation supervisor.
Kiisven was among six people who died in the crash involving a car and a lorry at 4am today.
The other fatalities were identified as car driver V. Mugilan, 25, and passengers K. Dineshvaran, 22, K. Alaganathan, 21, A. Kanabati Raja, 19, and M. Paranthaman, 16. The 31-year-old lorry driver sustained severe injuries.
Police said investigations revealed the car carrying the victims was travelling from Kuantan towards Kuala Lumpur when it went out of control while going downhill, veered into the opposing lane, and collided with the oncoming lorry. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sanusi claims Tanah Melayu remarks twisted for political gain, ready to take legal action
Article:
ALOR STAR: Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor insisted that his remarks on Tanah Melayu being the sole homeland for Malays, made during a ceramah in Negri Sembilan, had been twisted for political gain.
The Kedah Menteri Besar, who is also Perikatan Nasional election director, said he would take legal action, including filing lawsuits, against any individual or party that deliberately manipulated his remarks.
"I only stated facts. Anyone trying to manipulate this issue for political capital will be sued.
"I will lodge a counter police report. I will take legal action to set the record straight. Do not attempt to distort the facts," he said.
Sanusi said this after launching the state-level Animal Welfare Carnival, Malaya Sado Cattle Gathering and World Rabies Day celebration at Suka Menanti here today.
During a ceramah in Jempol on Thursday, Sanusi reportedly said that Malays had no other homeland, while Indians, Chinese, Cambodians and Thais each had countries associated with their ethnic groups.
Sanusi clarified that his remarks merely touched on historical facts, adding that his speech that evening was not directed at any specific individual.
"The details are clear. People are deliberately manipulating it. They take a portion of it, comment on it and add their own interpretations. Then they create an issue. That is all.
"Don't Malaysians understand the language? It is deliberately being blown out of proportion to gain political mileage and tarnish my image," he said, while stressing that history should not be used as a reason to create tension as it was a fact that needed to be studied to understand past events and plan for the future.
He added that those who circulated videos or reports that allegedly did not reflect his actual remarks should be held accountable for their actions.
"I do not know who they are. I do not even know those people. They are not popular. If they are seeking popularity through videos like these, what is the point?
"They sent videos saying that someone had lodged a police report. I will lodge a counter report if they distort what I said.
"I said something else, but they claimed I said something different. Say what is true. We do not need to be afraid as long as we are right. Those who are afraid are usually the ones who are in the wrong," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration detainees first to undergo Refugee Registration Document screening
Article:
PARIT BUNTAR: Immigration detainees nationwide will be the first group to undergo screening under the government's newly introduced Refugee Registration Document initiative.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the move would allow authorities to conduct comprehensive verification and security screening before deciding whether individuals claiming refugee status were eligible for recognition.
He said there were currently about 21,000 occupants at immigration depots nationwide, with around 4,000 claiming to be refugees.
"We have started the process. The first group being given attention are those currently housed at immigration depots.
"Once all processes are completed, the government itself will decide whether an individual is truly eligible to be granted refugee status or otherwise," he said.
Saifuddin told reporters after launching the Prisons Department's Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School programmes at Dewan PDT Tanjung Piandang here today.
Saifuddin said the introduction of the DPP was aimed at enabling Malaysia to establish its own refugee registration system instead of relying entirely on the refugee management process currently administered by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
"Are we fully satisfied with this method? We are not fully satisfied.
"That is why the government has taken a second approach, where we ourselves will carry out the refugee registration process. We have named this initiative the Refugee Registration Document," he said.
Under the initiative, he said, the government would collect comprehensive data on refugees, including their names, addresses, ages, gender, skills and biometric information such as facial recognition and iris scans.
He said holders of UNHCR cards were only exempted from action under the Immigration Act for offences related to overstaying and entering the country without valid documents.
"However, they are still subject to Malaysian laws for other criminal offences," he said.
Saifuddin said the options for refugees issued with the DPP would remain unchanged, including placement in a third country, repatriation when conditions in their home country improved, or deportation after serving a sentence if they were convicted of criminal offences in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan polls: BN 'copy-pasted' PH manifesto, says Aminuddin
Article:
PORT DICKSON: Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has claimed that the Barisan Nasional manifesto for the Negri Sembilan election largely copied initiatives previously introduced and implemented by the Pakatan Harapan (PH) state government under his leadership.
The caretaker menteri besar said his administration had fulfilled the promises made in PH's manifesto, proving that commitments once dismissed by critics had since become a reference point for BN's own manifesto.
"When we launched our manifesto before, they said my promises could never be fulfilled.
"Today, it is clear and proven that the manifesto I implemented has been copied and pasted by BN," he said when met at the Linggi operations room here.
Aminuddin also questioned BN's pledge to attract RM30 billion in investments over the next five years, describing the target as significantly lower than the state's current investment performance.
"What is disappointing is that their manifesto promises RM30 billion in investments.
"They are fully aware that this state recorded RM19.1 billion in investments last year alone.
"In the first half of this year, we have already achieved nearly RM13 billion. That already matches and exceeds what they are offering for the next five years," he said.
He said the state government is currently developing about 11 new industrial areas to attract more high-impact investments.
He said that once these industrial zones are completed, the government's focus would shift to attracting investors capable of creating higher-paying jobs for young people.
Responding to allegations of abandoned or delayed projects, Aminuddin acknowledged that some developments had encountered problems but stressed that similar issues had also occurred under previous administrations.
"I admit there are stalled projects. They may mention the hospital in Rembau.
"But let us remember that during the previous administration, there were also many stalled projects that remained unfinished.
"There are abandoned buildings in Seremban town. Whose administration was that under? It certainly wasn't mine," he said.
He added that stalled projects should not be used merely as political ammunition, and that greater attention should instead be given to efforts to attract more investment and drive development in the state.
Meanwhile, Aminuddin claimed that BN's manifesto failed to clearly explain how it intended to strengthen traditional institutions, including its proposal to review the allowance rates for those institutions.
It was reported yesterday that BN unveiled
its manifesto for the Negri Sembilan election
, built around nine thrusts, 88 action plans and 15 initiatives under the Salam Sejahtera Scheme.
BN deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had said that the manifesto, themed Hebatkan Semula Negri Sembilan: Kestabilan Dibina, Negeri Dijaga, Rakyat Dibela, Kemakmuran Dicipta, was formulated based on the coalition's experience in developing both the state and the nation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Halal certification opens wider market opportunities for entrepreneurs - Perlis Raja Muda
Article:
PADANG BESAR: Halal certification can enhance consumer confidence, strengthen brand reputation and open wider market opportunities for entrepreneurs, said Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail.
He said the certification reflected entrepreneurs' commitment to ensuring their products and services complied with Islamic requirements while meeting established quality, safety and hygiene standards
Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra urged entrepreneurs in the state to seize the opportunity to obtain halal certification as a strategic move to strengthen business competitiveness.
"I would like to emphasise that halal certification should be embraced as an act of worship carried out with sincerity, and upheld as a responsibility that requires integrity and accountability," he said when officiating the state-level T.A.A.T Zone Recognition Programme and Malaysia Halal Certification 2026 here today.
Also present was Raja Puan Muda of Perlis Tuanku Dr Hajah Lailatul Shahreen Akashah Khalil.
He said the authorities should continue playing a proactive role in facilitating entrepreneurs' efforts to encourage greater participation in halal certification applications, thereby strengthening the halal ecosystem in Perlis.
"I hope Perlis will continue to serve as an example in developing the country's halal ecosystem. The T.A.A.T Zone campaign should help raise awareness among food premise operators to practise the values of Tayyibah, Amanah, 'Afiyah and Taharah before applying for Malaysia Halal Certification," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Schoolgirls' families searched abandoned flats before bodies discovered
Article:
IPOH: Family members of two 14-year-old schoolgirls found dead at the abandoned Sungai Pari Flats in Buntong yesterday had searched for them at the site shortly before their bodies were discovered.
Security guard R. Madhesh, 22, said the brother of one of the victims arrived around 2.30pm with a friend on a motorcycle to look for his sister.
"About an hour later, the guardian of one of the girls arrived by car," he said.
Madhesh said he was away at a nearby shop when the bodies were discovered and was later informed by a colleague.
"The brother and his friend asked if I had seen two teenage girls entering the area. I said no, although his friend had said he saw them enter at 1.30pm.
"I then accompanied them in searching the area, but there was no response and we could not find the girls.
"About an hour later, the guardian arrived in tears and asked if I had seen the two girls," he said when met at the scene today.
Madhesh said he searched the abandoned flats again, including the upper floors, before his supervisor instructed him to come down and told the family to wait on the ground floor.
"I then went out to buy a drink. When I returned, a crowd had gathered around the bodies of the two teenagers," he said.
Meanwhile, resident Roshider Pal Singh Karam Singh, 46, said the Sungai Pari Flats had been abandoned for 13 years and were known locally as a hotspot for drug-related activities.
He said the site had also been used as a filming location for dramas and horror films.
"Previously, this area was used for drug transactions. I understand the land has since been purchased and the new owner plans to redevelop it without demolishing the existing structures, as this could risk causing cracks to nearby residents' homes," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prisons Dept taps inmates' TVET skills for community projects
Article:
PARIT BUNTAR: The Prisons Department is ready to collaborate with government ministries and agencies to utilise the skills of inmates undergoing Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) for community development projects.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the department's approach under the Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School programmes was unique, as it involved inmates, or prospects, in carrying out infrastructure projects for local communities.
Unlike other agencies that typically engage contractors, he said the Prisons Department mobilised prospects who had undergone skills training to contribute to such projects.
"The prospects are trained with TVET skills and then sent to villages to help complete projects.
"For example, at fishermen's jetties, they built ramps to allow boats to be moved up for cleaning. They were also involved in constructing toilets and asnaf houses," he said.
Saifuddin said this after launching the Prisons Department's Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School programmes at Dewan PDT Tanjung Piandang here today.
He said the programme was part of the Home Ministry's Madani initiative, with all 11 agencies under the ministry allocated funds to implement similar efforts.
For the Madani Adopted Village programme, Saifuddin said the Prisons Department received RM500,000, which was used to upgrade facilities, including mosques, surau, jetties, religious learning centres and asnaf houses.
Meanwhile, the Madani Adopted School programme received RM100,000.
He said the initiative not only provided immediate benefits to communities but also gave prospects an opportunity to apply the skills acquired during rehabilitation.
"The workforce comprises prospects who are currently undergoing training. This is the unique aspect of the Prisons Department's approach.
"By the end of the programme, the local community will benefit, whether it involves fishermen's associations, NGOs or asnaf groups," he said.
He said the Prisons Department remained open to collaborating with other ministries, departments and agencies that wished to utilise the skills of trained prospects for suitable projects.
"Should other agencies or ministries feel that the prospects we train can help complete their projects, the Prisons Department is always open to such cooperation," he said.
He added that, beyond the Madani Adopted Village programme, the department continued efforts to match trained prospects with employers.
Currently, he said 453 companies had expressed willingness to employ prospects trained by the department.
"Technically, they are still serving their sentences. However, during a certain period, they are placed outside prison institutions while remaining under the supervision of the Prisons Department.
"We match them with suitable companies and employers, and they receive salaries," he said.
He said prospects were trained in various skills, including welding, construction, painting, electrical wiring, weaving, songket production, carpentry and furniture-making.
He said such opportunities would help prospects rebuild their lives while reducing the stigma faced by former inmates.
"Imagine the parents' reaction. Their child entered prison after being convicted of an offence, but while in prison, we provide them with skills and they are able to generate income," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Bullying has no place in schools
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today voiced concern over bullying in schools, urging educators to treat every case seriously.
Anwar said he was deeply troubled whenever he was informed of bullying incidents, stressing that such behaviour was incompatible with the values the education system sought to instil.
"I am very uncomfortable whenever I hear of bullying cases in schools. We speak about reform, education and character, yet such incidents still occur among our children," he said at the official launching ceremony of SMKA Sheikh Tahir Jalaluddin here today.
While acknowledging that such cases did not involve the majority of students, Anwar said teachers and school administrators should never regard bullying as a minor issue.
"I hope teachers will not take this lightly because this problem exists in schools without exception," he said.
Anwar said some educators might be reluctant to publicise such cases to protect their schools' reputation, but stressed that this should never come at the expense of students' welfare.
"It is an injustice if a child is abused. It should never happen," he said.
He said education reform was not merely about improving academic achievement or school facilities, but also about nurturing values, discipline and good character.
Anwar said schools must ensure that students develop strong moral values alongside knowledge, noting that the true measure of education lay in producing individuals with integrity and compassion.
He added that meaningful change could only be achieved through knowledge, wisdom and good conduct, in line with the Madani government's aspiration to strengthen both educational excellence and character development.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: School liaison officers first point of contact for students, parents
Article:
PARIT BUNTAR: School liaison officers remain key to enhancing school safety.
They go beyond addressing bullying cases and serve as the first point of contact for students, parents and school authorities, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
Commenting on the recent deaths of two 14-year-old girls who were believed to have fallen from an abandoned residential building in Buntong, Ipoh, after reportedly leaving their school compound, Saifuddin said each case must be assessed based on its own facts before any conclusions are drawn.
He said the police, together with the National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada), had deployed liaison officers to schools nationwide to strengthen engagement and facilitate early intervention.
"We place school liaison officers in schools. It is not only the police, Nada also assigns officers.
"The purpose is for them to become the first point of contact for schools, parents and students, especially in cases involving bullying or other forms of harassment," he said.
She said this after opening the Prisons Department's Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School programmes at Dewan PDT Tanjung Piandang here today.
He said school safety encompasses a wide range of issues and should not be viewed solely through the lens of bullying.
"We have to look at every case based on the facts. A few weeks ago, there was an incident in Padang Terap, Kedah, involving a student who fell from a school building. Initial reports simply stated that a student had fallen.
"However, police investigations found that eyewitnesses saw the student attempting to retrieve a bird's nest from the school roof before slipping.
"In such circumstances, the incident was beyond the control or reach of the school liaison officer," he said.
She said school liaison officers regularly conduct awareness talks and educational programmes to educate students on personal safety and appropriate behaviour in school.
"If such incidents continue to occur, it underscores the need for cooperation from all parties, including school authorities, the police, Parent-Teacher Associations and parents.
"Students must also be continuously exposed to awareness programmes on personal safety in school. That is the most practical approach," he said.
When asked whether school liaison officers were assigned only to selected schools, Saifuddin said police had profiled schools according to their respective risk levels.
"Police have mapped schools based on their risk profiles. We know the issues faced by each school, whether they involve truancy, gangsterism or other problems affecting students.
"The appointment of school liaison officers is determined by the police in cooperation with the respective schools, and the programme is already being implemented," he said.
Earlier, Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said police officers had been assigned to all 10,255 schools under the Education Ministry, comprising 2,481 secondary schools and 7,774 primary schools.
Previously,
Saifuddin
said schools must remain free from negative elements, including drug abuse, banned substances, bullying and gangsterism, which could jeopardise students' safety and development.
Following this, the ministry has taken steps to station school liaison officers at selected schools to address these issues.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Nazrin presents Perak King's Scout Awards
Article:
IPOH: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Shah today graced the presentation of the King's Scout Award, decorations, medals and certificates for the state's Scouts Association of Malaysia (PPM) branch.
Also present were Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and National Chief Scout Maj-Gen Prof Datuk Mohd Zin Bidin.
A total of 239 recipients received awards from Sultan Nazrin.
Among them was Head of the Regional Scout Council (Kwarda) of the Special Region of Yogyakarta, Gusti Kanjeng Ratu Mangkubumi Hamemayu Hayuning Bawono Langgeng Ing Mataram, who was conferred the Bintang Semangat Rimba Emas (BSR-E).
The BSR-E is the third-highest award of the Scouts Association of Malaysia, presented to individuals who have rendered distinguished service to the scout movement.
In his speech, Mohd Zin said the association was entering a new phase of transformation that is bolder, more modern and forward-looking.
He said Malaysia's standing on the global stage had been strengthened with Kuala Lumpur serving as the headquarters of the World Scout Bureau.
"This places Malaysia at the heart of the global scouting network, creating opportunities for the exchange of expertise, the sharing of best practices and broader collaboration with the worldwide scout fraternity," he said.
Mohd Zin said the association's transformation — including its rebranding exercise, new logo and redesigned uniform — represented more than a cosmetic change, reflecting its confidence in facing future challenges with renewed energy and aspirations.
On the Perak branch, he noted that 2026 marks the association's centenary.
"The 100th anniversary of Perak Scouts is a celebration of a century of service and a renewed commitment to continue serving the nation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former COO loses unfair dismissal claim over 'stealth' company venture
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former chief operating officer earning RM50,000 a month has lost his unfair dismissal claim after the Industrial Court upheld his termination over setting up and operating a separate company in "stealth" while still employed.
Industrial Court chairman Chow Siew Lin ruled that Advent Packaging Sdn Bhd had just cause to dismiss Ooi Tse Biing after finding that he had set up and operated SG Film Sdn Bhd (SG Film) without the company's consent and authorisation, breaching his employment contract.
Ooi, who earned RM50,000 a month as the company's chief operating officer (COO), claimed he had been unfairly dismissed. He was terminated on Jan 21, 2024 on grounds of misconduct. He had began serving as COO in August 2019.
According to the court document, Ooi's dismissal arose from his alleged misconduct as the COO by setting up another company, SG Film Sdn Bhd (SG Film), "without the consent and authorisation of the company while he was still employed."
On whether the misconduct complained of by the company had been established, Chow said: "This court agrees with the company's contention that the misconduct complained of is not premised solely on the setting up of a competitor company; rather, it concerns Ooi's unauthorised acts of setting up and subsequently the operations of SG Film in stealth."
Ooi received RM10,000 in management fees and RM20,000 in consultancy fees from SG Film while still employed by Advent Packaging, according to the court document.
Chow said Ooi had admitted receiving the above sums of money from SG Film while he was still an employee of the company.
"He had further testified that he had kept the money and did not give it to the company."
Chow said: "What Ooi had done was against the company's best interest and simply points to a blatant breach of his fiduciary duty to the company."
In its award, the court found that Ooi had breached both the express and implied terms of his contract of service, particularly the conflict of interest provision, and that his conduct was incompatible with the fiduciary relationship between him and the company.
The court said Ooi had misplaced the trust reposed in him by the company and that his actions amounted to a serious breach of his duty of confidentiality and good faith, destroying the trust and confidence necessary to sustain the employment relationship.
It ruled that no reasonable employer could be expected to retain an employee whose misconduct was of such gravity.
The court also held that summary dismissal was proportionate to the severity of Ooi's misconduct and found no reason to disturb Advent Packaging's decision to terminate his employment.
Chow said: "Based on the totality of the evidence adduced by both parties as well as the submissions made without regard to technicalities and legal form as provided under Section 30(5) of the Act, this court holds that the punishment of dismissal was warranted and the claimant's dismissal was with just cause or excuse."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asyraf Wajdi demands RM5mil over alleged defamation linking him to TH
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki is seeking RM5 million in damages from two individuals whom he accused of defaming him by linking him to an issue involving Tabung Haji.
In a Facebook post, Asyraf said he had instructed his lawyer, Datuk Adnan Seman, to issue letters of demand (LOD) to Amanah central leadership council member Datuk Dr Ismail Salleh and social media account owner Abied Abdullah over the alleged defamatory claims.
He said the LODs demanded that both individuals publicly apologise, retract the alleged defamatory statements, provide an undertaking and pay RM5 million in damages.
"I have instructed my lawyer, Adnan, to issue LODs against Ismail and the owner of the Abied Abdullah account (Habin Faisal Mohamed) for defaming, humiliating and tarnishing my reputation, as well as attempting to link me to the TH issue.
"The demands include an apology, retraction of the statements, an undertaking and RM5 million in damages. If they fail to comply, a lawsuit will be filed," he said in the post.
Asyraf said the action was taken following allegations that the two individuals had circulated statements that tarnished his reputation and dignity by linking him to the TH issue.
He added that if he succeeds in the defamation suit, he would donate the entire amount of damages received to Yayasan Pelajaran Mara to help students from underprivileged families pursue their education.
"God willing, if I win this defamation suit, I promise and am determined to channel every sen received to Yayasan Pelajaran Mara to help poor and underprivileged students continue their studies," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police open 11 investigation papers over election offences in Negri Sembilan
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan police have opened 11 investigation papers and received 16 reports regarding alleged election-related offences in the state polls, including two opened yesterday.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said one investigation paper opened yesterday was under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, resulting in property loss or damage.
"Another investigation paper was opened under Section 505 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for issuing, creating, publishing or disseminating statements, rumours or news that could cause public mischief," he said in a statement today.
However, Alzafny said the overall security and public order situation throughout the election process remained good and under control.
"The public is urged to continue complying with the law, respect the democratic process, and provide full cooperation to police on the ground to ensure the Negri Sembilan election takes place in a peaceful, harmonious, and orderly manner," he said.
He added that police approved 322 of the 345 applications to hold ceramah and campaign activities between July 18 and yesterday.
He said police monitored all approved political programmes and activities to ensure compliance with the law without compromising public safety and order.
Early voting for the state election is scheduled for July 28, while polling day is Aug 1.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN manifesto offers practical roadmap for Negri's revival, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Barisan Nasional's manifesto for the Negri Sembilan election offers a practical and realistic blueprint to revive programmes that were left unfinished after BN lost power, says chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the manifesto, launched by state BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan last night, was built on foundations laid during BN's previous administration and could be implemented immediately should the coalition return to power.
"The manifesto is very good. Tok Mat, as Negri Sembilan BN chairman, underlined that it is a continuation of programmes introduced previously but which were disrupted over the past two terms.
"Whoever leads Negri Sembilan after the election should take into account what has been outlined in the BN manifesto.
"We had already laid a strong foundation before this, but because we did not have enough seats to form the government, those programmes could not be carried out," he said after attending the Salam Agrikomoditi Madani programme at Dataran Melang.
He said if voters gave BN another mandate, the coalition would proceed with implementing the initiatives that had been put on hold.
"If God wills it and the people decide to place their trust in BN again, then these programmes will be carried out as a continuation of what was left unfinished.
"I believe the BN manifesto offers the most practical proposals because the groundwork is already there and they are achievable.
"I am confident Negri Sembilan can record economic growth above the national average, God willing," he said.
Yesterday, BN launched its manifesto for the 16th Negri Sembilan election, outlining 88 initiatives anchored on nine key thrusts.
The manifesto also includes 15 Salam Sejahtera Scheme initiatives, as well as the establishment of a Manifesto Implementation Monitoring and Coordination Unit should BN be given the mandate in the state election scheduled for Aug 1.
Separately, Zahid said there was no reason for non-Malay voters to be concerned about what has been described as the "Blue Wave" in the state election.
He said BN remained a multiracial coalition comprising parties representing various communities, and therefore posed no threat to any ethnic group.
"The 'blue wave' is Barisan Nasional's wave.
"BN includes Chinese and Indian-based parties. There is no reason for Chinese, Indians, Orang Asli, or voters from Sabah and Sarawak living in Negri Sembilan to feel doubtful or uneasy. I do not believe that issue arises," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 144,894 smallholders approved for Budi Agrikomoditi assistance, says minister
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad said a total of 144,894 smallholders had been approved to receive the Budi Agrikomoditi assistance scheme as of July 15.
Noraini said the figure was the highest number of approvals recorded by any ministry under the government's targeted diesel subsidy initiative.
She said there could still be eligible smallholders who had yet to register or were unfamiliar with the application process.
"To date, our ministry has recorded the highest number of approved smallholders.
"This is an achievement we are proud of, but we cannot be complacent. There may still be eligible smallholders who have not registered or do not fully understand the application process," she said while speaking at the Salam Agrikomoditi Madani programme at Dataran Melang today.
The programme was officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Noraini said the ministry also provided information on the Budi Agrikomoditi scheme throughout the programme.
"We are providing information on Budi Agrikomoditi. This targeted subsidy initiative helps eligible farmers and commodity smallholders reduce part of their diesel costs for agricultural activities and commodity production," she said.
She said the Salam Agrikomoditi programme was introduced with the simple aim of bringing the ministry closer to the people.
"We realise that many people are still unfamiliar with the role of the ministry and its agencies. Some are unaware of the assistance available.
"Some want to undergo training but do not know where to begin. Others already run businesses but are still looking for guidance on how to expand further.
"Sometimes the opportunities are there and the information is available, but the gap between the community and government agencies means these opportunities are not fully utilised.
"That is why we do not want to simply wait for people to come to the ministry. We are going out to meet them," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia women-only trains gain global attention after French documentary feature
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's public rail network has captured international attention after being featured in the French travel documentary series Des trains pas comme les autres (Amazing Train Journeys).
In a video clip that went viral online, the documentary showcased Kuala Lumpur's designated women-only coaches, drawing praise from local commuters and international viewers.
"In the Kuala Lumpur metro in Malaysia, certain carriages are reserved exclusively for women. Marked by pink stripes, they offer a space where women can travel with greater peace of mind," the official episode description read.
Malaysian netizens took to social media platforms to express their support for the initiative, highlighting how the designated coaches enhance daily commutes.
On Threads, user @cik.kentangbatu shared that the women-only carriages were practical for peak-hour travel.
"The women's coach is so practical when commuting to work. Even if we have to squeeze against other women, it doesn't matter. I feel safe, and women support one another even if they are complete strangers," she wrote.
Another user, @damien_mikeng, said the initiative reflected Malaysia's cultural values.
"Culturally, Malaysians of all races and religions naturally observe personal boundaries between genders," he posted.
Echoing similar sentiments, user @fauzanizam succinctly added that the initiative fundamentally boiled down to "providing comfort and safety".
[[nid:1496781]]
The documentary feature also sparked a broader global conversation on Facebook, with international viewers pointing out that women-only public transport initiatives exist worldwide as a practical courtesy.
Facebook user Martine Carlier noted: "In Mexico, there have been pink buses reserved for women and their children for years."
Meanwhile, another commenter, Olivier Noirot-Cosson, said such measures transcended culture and religion.
"Nothing extraordinary, and nothing to do with religion. When I went to England in the 1970s, there were 'women only' compartments. It is simply about respect and comfort," he shared.
Women-only coaches were first introduced on Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd's trains in 2010, before being expanded to the MRT Kajang Line and MRT Putrajaya Line by Prasarana Malaysia Bhd to provide a safer and more comfortable travel experience for female passengers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'No need to come to Negri': Zahid tells Sanusi to focus on Kedah, avoid divisive rhetoric
Article:
KUALA PILAH: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has cautioned Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor not to stir up racial and religious sensitivities in Negri Sembilan ahead of its state election.
Zahid said the Kedah menteri besar should stay in Kedah for the remainder of the campaign period and focus on governing his state instead of campaigning in Negri Sembilan.
"We still have six more days of campaigning. It would be better for him to keep himself busy governing Kedah," Zahid said after attending the Salam Agrikomoditi Madani programme at Dataran Melang.
"I don't think there is any need for him to come to Negri Sembilan. Let us manage Negri Sembilan in our own way."
Zahid added that he did not intend to advise Sanusi, but merely remind him to watch his words.
"Even if there is a tiger in his heart, when he speaks, let only the goat come out," he said.
"I do not want any interpretation that could end up causing unease among various groups in society.
"If his intention is to show unity among the ummah, there is no need to touch on issues involving ethnicity, religion, culture or the background of other races in this country."
Zahid's remarks came after a news portal reported that Sanusi, during a ceramah in Jempol, said Malays had no other homeland, while Indians, Chinese, Cambodians, and Thais each had countries associated with their ethnic groups.
Zahid said that Malaysia's diversity was part of its natural social fabric and should not be exploited for political gain.
"I have confidence in the country's plural society. This diversity is sunnatullah (God's ordained order).
"There is no need to raise such matters. If they truly want to build friendships, then do so properly, not by bringing up other issues," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar rejects Sanusi's 'Tanah Melayu' remarks, says Malaysia must embrace all citizens
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's remarks on Tanah Melayu, saying Malaysia's strength lies in embracing all citizens.
Anwar said Malaysia, independent for nearly 70 years, should not have leaders making statements that could insult or exclude other communities.
He said while Malays were historically associated with Tanah Melayu, Malaysia's citizens came from diverse ancestral backgrounds and all who accepted the Constitution and contributed to the country must be regarded as part of the nation.
"Malays, the majority of whom originated from Tanah Melayu, also include those with roots from Indonesia. There are also those of Chinese and Korean descent, and we cannot reject them as not being rakyat," he said.
He was responding to remarks by Sanusi during the Perikatan Nasional (PN) campaign for the Negri Sembilan state election, where the coalition used racial and religious rhetoric, including suggesting that different ethnic groups in Malaysia could fall back on ancestral homelands outside the country.
On Thursday, Sanusi, who is also PN election director, said Tanah Melayu was the only homeland for Malays, unlike other ethnic groups who, he claimed, could return to countries such as India, China or Thailand.
He also claimed Malay political power and economic control were increasingly being eroded and could disappear within 10 years without drastic changes.
Anwar said such views were unacceptable, stressing that Malaysians from all communities who uphold the Federal Constitution and contribute to the nation must be embraced.
"Especially among the Chinese and Indian communities, who are loyal, accept the Constitution and are good citizens, we must embrace them as Malaysia's strength," he said after the launch of SMKA Sheikh Tahir Jalaluddin here today.
"I do not agree at all with any perception that insults or sidelines the role of any community in our country," he added.
Anwar said Malaysia's diversity should be viewed as a source of strength rather than a basis for division.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke urges NS election rivals to campaign positively, avoid arrogance
Article:
JELEBU: All parties contesting the Negri Sembilan election should campaign positively and avoid arrogant statements
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the ultimate decision on the fate of any candidate or party rested entirely with the voters.
"There is no need for us, as cabinet partners, to be arrogant. We should campaign positively.
"Whether someone gets defeated or not is up to the people, because the voters are the ones who will decide.
"The local people know better than Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid. If he says there has been no development, the Chennah state constituency is also under the Jelebu parliamentary constituency.
"So who holds the Jelebu parliamentary seat? There's no need to be arrogant," he told reporters after a walkabout at the Titi morning market today.
Yesterday, Zahid said that if BN wins the Chennah and Linggi state seats in this election, it would succeed in wresting control of Negri Sembilan from Pakatan Harapan.
He said the objective centres on the Chennah and Linggi state constituencies, where Loke and Negri Sembilan PH chairman Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun are contesting, respectively.
Commenting on facilities in Chennah, Loke said the rural constituency has received various improvements and infrastructure upgrades for the benefit and comfort of residents.
He said development in the area is a shared responsibility since Chennah falls under the administration of the Jelebu parliamentary constituency.
"The people know better, and I will continue to remain positive and campaign positively. We will continue appealing to voters to support PH so that we can keep serving them.
"The voters here know me, and I will continue engaging with people from all communities — Malay, Chinese, Indian, as well as the Orang Asli," he said.
Loke also rejected claims by some parties and media analyses suggesting that the combined vote share of BN and Perikatan Nasional in the 15th General Election reached 58 per cent in Chennah.
"That's not accurate. Since becoming the elected representative here, I have consistently received more than 50 per cent of the vote since 2013. So some of those figures are actually incorrect," he said.
On the increasingly intense second week of campaigning, with Chennah being labelled one of the election's "hot seats," Loke said such a situation is normal in any election.
"Yes, every seat is a hot seat. Which election isn't competitive? We will campaign calmly and continue to stay calm.
"The response to PH has been quite good so far. We are using different approaches depending on the area, including holding meetings in villages. With one week of campaigning remaining, we will continue to build on this positive momentum," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China evacuates 20,000 people as Typhoon Noul nears
Article:
BEIJING: Authorities have evacuated more than 20,000 people and suspended railway services in southern China as Typhoon Noul approaches, threatening torrential rain and gale-force winds, according to state media.
The typhoon is forecast to make landfall along the coastal area stretching from Hong Kong to Guangdong province between Saturday evening and Sunday morning, China's National Meteorological Center said.
It maintained an orange typhoon alert on Saturday, the second-highest level in its four-tier warning system, after warning that parts of Guangdong and neighbouring Fujian province would experience gales and torrential rain.
More than 20,000 people had been evacuated in Guangdong, state broadcaster CCTV said in a bulletin late on Friday.
Fishing vessels operating at sea in the province had returned to port to shelter from the storm, it added.
Guangdong will suspend some train services on Saturday morning, with all rail services in the province to be halted on Sunday, CCTV said.
Schools in Guangdong's Chaozhou city were instructed to suspend on-campus activities, according to local media reports.
Extreme weather has already wreaked havoc on southern and central China this month, with 39 people killed when Typhoon Maysak triggered devastating floods in Guangxi.
Maysak also caused thunderstorms and gale-force winds that killed 11 people and injured 331 in the central province of Hubei.
Scientists warn that the intensity and frequency of extreme weather events worldwide will increase as the planet continues to warm because of fossil fuel emissions.
China is the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases, but it is also a global renewable energy powerhouse that aims to make its massive economy carbon neutral by 2060.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt absorbs higher oil costs to keep RON95 at RM1.99, says Anwar
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH: Malaysia is maintaining the RON95 petrol price at RM1.99 despite rising global oil prices by spending up to RM50 billion a year on fuel subsidies, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar said the government continued to shield consumers from higher fuel costs by absorbing billions of ringgit in subsidies, even as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pushed up crude oil prices and import costs.
"Alhamdulillah, despite all these challenges, Malaysia is still able to maintain the RON95 price at RM1.99 and diesel at RM2.10.
"But the government has to pay for it. It is not free. People think RM1.99 is the actual market price, but it is not. The government bears the difference," he said when closing National Training Week 2026 here today.
Anwar said crude oil prices, which were projected at about US$70 per barrel when the government prepared the Budget, had since climbed to between US$80 and US$85 per barrel and, at one point, reached US$100 following the conflict involving Iran and disruptions affecting the Strait of Hormuz.
Although Petronas produced part of the country's fuel supply, Malaysia still imported about half of its petroleum requirements, leaving it exposed to higher global prices.
Anwar said Putrajaya was expected to spend between RM40 billion and RM50 billion annually on fuel subsidies to keep pump prices low.
This was in addition to RM15 billion to RM16 billion allocated for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah programmes, as well as RM18 billion a year for civil service salary increases.
"These measures underscore the government's commitment to protecting Malaysians from rising living costs while maintaining fiscal discipline and implementing economic reforms," he added.
Anwar said he was not complaining but merely wanted people to understand.
"This money comes from government revenue and taxes," he said.
Despite the mounting fiscal commitments, Anwar said the government would continue to balance sound public finances with measures to ease the cost of living while pursuing reforms to strengthen Malaysia's economy.
He said the country's economic fundamentals remained strong, citing a stronger ringgit, record investment inflows and one of the highest growth rates in Asia as evidence that the government's reform agenda was delivering results.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man arrested over seditious, insulting Facebook post against Islam
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested a man for allegedly uploading a Facebook post containing seditious and insulting remarks against Islam.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report was lodged at 12.38am yesterday after a member of the public spotted the viral post on social media.
"Checks showed that the owner of a Facebook account under the name 'Fadzil Zahari' shared several screenshots believed to have been uploaded by account owner 'Parthiban Ragu', which contained statements insulting Islam as well as offensive and obscene expressions directed at Allah SWT and Prophet Muhammad SAW.
"Acting on information, a team of officers arrested a 37-year-old man at 1am today in Iskandar Puteri," he said in a statement.
He said checks revealed the suspect had no prior criminal record, adding that police seized two mobile phones to assist in the investigation.
The suspect was brought to the Johor Baru magistrate's court, where a four-day remand order was granted until Tuesday.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 298 of the Penal Code.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib Razak undergoes coronary procedure; no stent needed, doctors confirm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Former Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak is in stable condition and recovering after undergoing a coronary angiogram today, with doctors confirming that no further surgical intervention, such as balloon angioplasty or stent implantation, is required.
According to a statement released by his legal counsel, Messrs Shafee & Co., the medical procedure was deemed necessary following a series of health evaluations over the past several weeks. During these assessments, physicians detected a blockage in a coronary blood vessel that required further investigation via an angiogram.
The medical team had previously advised that there was an estimated 95% probability that Najib would require further intervention. However, following the completion of the angiogram and a comprehensive clinical evaluation today, attending specialists concluded that the blockage can be effectively managed through medication, ongoing monitoring, and regular follow-up care.
“The decision to proceed with today’s procedure was made entirely based on medical necessity and the clinical findings available at that time,” the statement read. “Given the high probability that further intervention would be required, the concerns regarding the procedure were real and justified. Fortunately, the coronary angiogram has shown that the blockage can be controlled without the need for balloon angioplasty or stent placement.”
The legal team emphasised that Najib, who is currently serving a prison sentence, is now in good condition and will continue his recovery process under the close supervision of his doctors.
The family extended their deepest gratitude to the cardiologists, cardiothoracic specialists, nurses, and the entire medical team at the Cardiothoracic and Cardiology Centre of Sultan Idris Shah Hospital in Serdang for their professionalism, expertise, and dedicated care throughout the process.
The statement also conveyed the family’s heartfelt appreciation to the Malaysian public for their prayers, well-wishes, and continued support during this health scare.
“Alhamdulillah, with the grace of Allah SWT, Dato’ Sri Najib is now in good condition and will continue his recovery process under the close supervision of the attending doctors,” the statement concluded.
The news comes as Najib continues to serve his sentence related to the SRC International case, with health concerns having previously led to several court postponements and hospitalisations in the past.

Title: Family, including baby, rescued from Tanjung Kling flash floods
Article:
MELAKA, July 25 — A family of three, including a four-month-old baby boy, were rescued after being trapped in flash floods at Kampung Lereh, Tanjung Kling here this morning.
Melaka Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) public relations officer Mohd Hafidzatullah Rashid said seven firefighters from the Tangga Batu Fire and Rescue Station were deployed after the department received an emergency call at 9.47am.
“The victims were safely evacuated before being handed over to the Village Development and Security Committee (JPKK) for further action,” he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, Melaka Civil Defence Force (APM) director Lt Col (PA) Kamarulsyah Muslim said continuous heavy rain since 1 am caused several flood-prone areas in Melaka Tengah to be inundated.
The affected areas included Peringgit in the Pengkalan Batu state constituency, as well as Kampung Kolam Limbungan and Tengkera in the Kesidang state constituency.
Kamarulsyah, who is also the State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) Secretariat spokesperson, said no temporary relief centre had been opened and no victims evacuated as of 10 am.
“Monitoring by agencies under JPBN and the District Disaster Management Committee (JPBD) is ongoing,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Police launch 16 probes into alleged election-related offences in Negeri Sembilan
Article:
SEREMBAN, July 25 — Negeri Sembilan police have received 16 reports and opened 11 investigation papers, including two opened yesterday, over alleged election-related offences in the state polls.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said one investigation paper opened yesterday was under Section 435 of the Penal Code for committing mischief by fire, resulting in the loss or damage of property.
“Another investigation paper was opened under Section 505 of the Penal Code/Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588) for issuing, creating, publishing or disseminating statements, rumours or news that could cause public mischief,” he said in a statement today.
However, Alzafny said the security and public order situation throughout the election process remained good and under control.
“The public is urged to continue complying with the law, respect the democratic process and provide full cooperation to police on the ground to ensure the Negeri Sembilan state election takes place in a peaceful, harmonious and orderly manner,” he said.
He also said police had approved 322 of the 345 applications to hold ceramah and other campaign activities for the period from July 18 until yesterday.
He said all approved political programmes and activities were monitored by police to ensure they complied with the law and did not compromise public safety and order.
Early voting for the state election is scheduled for July 28, while polling day is Aug 1.
For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9. — Bernama

Title: Melaka floods: Emergency shelters set up after relentless rain
Article:
MELAKA, July 25 —Two temporary relief centres have been opened after heavy rain caused flooding in several areas in the Melaka Tengah and Jasin districts as of 3 pm today.
In a statement, the Melaka State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the relief centre at the Pantai Kundor State Legislative Assembly Development and Coordination Committee (Japerun) was opened at 11.32 am and is sheltering 15 evacuees from seven families.
“The relief centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan Serkam Darat was opened at 1.25 pm and is still in the process of registering evacuees,” it said today.
Continuous heavy rain since early this morning has caused flooding in several areas in Melaka Tengah, namely Kampung Lereh, Peringgit, Kampung Bachang, Kampung Kolam Limbongan, Tengkera, Bukit Rambai, Tanjung Kling, Pengkalan Perigi and Kampung Berlian.
In Jasin, the affected villages are Kampung Pulai, Kampung Serkam and Kampung Bukit Tembakau.  — Bernama

Title: Suspect arrested in Shah Alam for armed van heist attempt
Article:
SHAH ALAM, July 25 —The male suspect in the attempted robbery of a security van and the theft of firearms in front of a bank in Bukit Tinggi, Klang, on Monday has been remanded for six days to assist in the investigation.
South Klang district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the remand application for the local suspect in his 20s, was made at the Klang Court yesterday.
“The court then granted the suspect a six-day remand starting yesterday until July 29,” he said via a Whatsapp message today.
Earlier, Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M Kumar said the local suspect, in his 20s, was arrested in Shah Alam, Selangor at 11 am, July 23.
He said in the July 20 incident, the suspect was believed to have tried to rob a security company vehicle that was carrying cash before seizing the security guard’s pump gun and fleeing on a motorcycle.
He said the case is currently being investigated under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code and Section 4 of the Firearms (Heavier Penalties) Act 1971. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan cooperation with Perikatan does not bind BN, says Ahmad Maslan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Barisan Nasional’s cooperation with Perikatan Nasional in the Negeri Sembilan state election is only a political understanding and does not amount to a formal agreement, Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said.
According to
Utusan Malaysia
